NoteTexAccessor::strip_macro¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_macro(std::string_view name) const

Remove One Macro’s Declarations¶

strip_macro(name) removes complete declarations of one control-word name from each cell. It recognizes \newcommand, \renewcommand, \providecommand, and primitive \def declarations, including parameter specifications and balanced nested bodies. Use it when a local definition must be discarded while declarations of other macros and all ordinary source remain.

name accepts RR or \RR; both identify the same control word. ASCII letters and @ are valid, with an optional terminal *. Empty names, spaces, punctuation, and embedded backslashes reject before any cell is transformed. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. The declaration disappears, but use sites such as \RR{x} remain unchanged: this is declaration removal, not macro expansion. Use macro_subs() to expand local definitions before discarding them.

Malformed declarations are retained. Complete declarations of other names are also retained. Removed regions are replaced by spacing, then ASCII whitespace is collapsed and cells are trimmed. The result is out-of-place, shape preserving, and idempotent for one name. Undefined state propagates only after the name passes validation; defined non-Text input rejects. Runtime is linear in source bytes, with balanced-group memory proportional to nesting depth.

Example 1: Declaration Families, Parameters, And Use Sites¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \newcommand{\RR}[1]{\mathbf{R}_{#1}} B \RR{x} C)",
    R"(\def\RR#1{{#1,#1}} \renewcommand{\ZZ}{Z} \RR{q})",
    R"(\\newcommand{\RR}{escaped} \newcommand{\RR}{unfinished)"});
const auto clean = source.tex().strip_macro("RR");
std::cout << clean << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A B \\RR{x} C", "\\renewcommand{\\ZZ}{Z} \\RR{q}", "\\\\newcommand{\\RR}{escaped} \\newcommand{\\RR}{unfinished"]

The RR declarations disappear; RR use sites and the complete ZZ declaration remain. Escaped and incomplete declaration text is preserved.

Example 2: A Leading Backslash Is An Equivalent Name Spelling¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \newcommand{\RR}[1]{\mathbf{R}_{#1}} B \RR{x} C)",
    R"(\def\RR#1{{#1,#1}} \renewcommand{\ZZ}{Z} \RR{q})",
    R"(\\newcommand{\RR}{escaped} \newcommand{\RR}{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_macro(R"(\RR)") << '\n';
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "same="
          << ((source.tex().strip_macro("RR") ==
               source.tex().strip_macro(R"(\RR)")).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A B \\RR{x} C", "\\renewcommand{\\ZZ}{Z} \\RR{q}", "\\\\newcommand{\\RR}{escaped} \\newcommand{\\RR}{unfinished"]
same=true

Example 3: Invalid Names Reject Before Reading Input¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_macro("bad name");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip_macro(bad name): rejected\n";
}

Output¶

strip_macro(bad name): rejected

Example 4: Undefined State, Dtype, And Idempotence¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(A \newcommand{\RR}{\mathbb{R}} B \RR C)");
const auto once = source.tex().strip_macro("RR");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((once == once.tex().strip_macro("RR")).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_macro("RR").defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1})
      .tex().strip_macro("RR");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip macro Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
strip macro Int64: rejected
